text: Then Zophar the Naamathite answered:
"Should such a flood of words go unanswered? Is a man proved right just because he talks?
Should your empty talk silence others? Are you to mock with no one to rebuke you?
You say, 'My teaching is pure, and I am clean in your sight.'
But oh, that God himself would speak, that he would open his lips against you,
and disclose to you the secrets of wisdom—for sound understanding has two sides. Then you would know that God has overlooked much of your guilt.
Can you fathom the depths of God? Can you probe the limits of the Almighty?
Higher than the heavens—what can you do? Deeper than the grave—what can you know?

versions.text: They are higher than the heavens—what can you do? Deeper than the grave—what can you know?
versions.explanation: The pronoun "They" has no clear antecedent in the preceding line (which speaks of God and the Almighty in the singular), which is confusing when read aloud. The Hebrew has no pronoun; dropping it keeps the terse, exclamatory rhythm of the original.

text: Its measure is longer than the earth and wider than the sea.

versions.text: Their measure is longer than the earth and wider than the sea.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew suffix on מִדָּהּ is feminine singular, matching the singular idea of God's greatness/wisdom; "Their" carries over the unclear plural pronoun from the previous line.

text: If he sweeps through and imprisons, if he convenes the court, who can turn him back?
For he knows those who are worthless; he sees their wickedness—should he not take note of it?
But a hollow man will gain understanding about as soon as a wild donkey is born human.
If you would set your heart right and stretch out your hands to him,
if you put away the sin that is in your hand and let no wrongdoing dwell in your tents,
then you could lift up your face without shame; you would stand firm and be unafraid.
You would forget your misery, remembering it like waters that have flowed away.
Your life would be brighter than noon, and darkness would become like morning.
You would rest secure, for there is hope; you would look around and lie down in safety.
You would rest with no one to make you afraid, and many would seek your favor.

versions.text: You would lie down with no one to make you afraid, and many would seek your favor.
versions.explanation: "Lie down" repeats the identical wording at the end of the previous verse, which sounds monotonous in oral reading; the Hebrew uses a different verb here (רבץ rather than שכב), so a slight variation better reflects the original.

text: But the eyes of the wicked will fail; every escape will be cut off from them, and their hope will be the last gasp of breath."
